name: DENSHŌ
subtitle: Stories of craftsmanship.
meaning: 伝承 — the handing down of something, from one pair of hands to the next.
standfirst: People who have given their lives to making, and the worlds that have grown around their work.
introduction: DENSHŌ follows people who dedicate themselves to craft — to a material, a technique, a discipline that takes decades to learn and a lifetime to keep. Some of them work in traditions older than the countries they live in. Some are the last to hold a particular piece of knowledge. Most of them do not think of themselves as remarkable.

The series is less interested in objects than in the lives around them: the hours, the rooms, the families, the compromises, the reasons someone chooses to keep doing something the slow way in a world that has stopped asking for it. What is being handed down is rarely just a skill. It is a way of paying attention.
Each entry follows one place and the people met there. The numbering runs within the series, in the order the work was made.
